item.title: Backup for Freedom: OVHcloud Backup Center runs on Plakar
item.description: OVHcloud presented Backup Center at its AI Summit: native backup for Public Cloud, built on the open-source Plakar engine. Managed Kubernetes comes first, with a free Beta and general availability in early 2027.

item.title: How to backup and restore PVCs with the Kubernetes Operator
item.description: An 18-minute walkthrough of the Plakar Kubernetes Operator: WordPress and MariaDB on EKS, backed up to S3 and restored, every step declared in YAML.

item.title: Free backup for KubeVirt VMs and OpenShift
item.description: Plakar’s Kubernetes integration now backs up KubeVirt VMs: every disk plus the VM manifest, in one consistent snapshot. On OpenShift, a new openshift package keeps restores from doing things you didn’t ask for. Both are free.

item.title: Resilience as Code, because backup should be Infrastructure.
item.description: Backup is the last layer of your stack still clicked into a console. The Plakar Kubernetes Operator makes it code: declare resilience as Custom Resources, reconciled from Git, for everything you run.

item.title: Backing up kubernetes clusters with Plakar
item.description: We built a Kubernetes integration for Plakar that backs up clusters at three levels: etcd (disaster recovery), manifests (granular restore and inspection), and persistent volumes (via CSI snapshots). This enables full cluster recovery, fine-grained restores, and data portability across environments.
